title: THE SPARK · A+A SNATCH REPEATS + THE FURNACE
vibe: green · hard · 45 minutes · power measured in how fast you recover, not in how wrecked you get
why: Seven hours, nothing sore, legs tired, and you want to go hard. Read that carefully, because it points somewhere specific. Tired legs plus a hard day is not a contradiction, it is a request for the effort to come from somewhere other than your quads and your feet. Yesterday was twenty-four get-ups and three rounds of carries and crawls, all of it slow, all of it grinding, none of it fast. Scroll further back and the gap is glaring: there has been no ballistic work, no snatch, no explosive hip in this log since 08-01. Power is the single most neglected quality you own right now, and power is exactly the quality that does not care that your legs are tired, because it is produced in about six seconds and paid for by resting. So today is a power day, and it borrows an organizing principle this program has never once used. StrongFirst calls it A plus A, alactic plus aerobic. The idea is the inverse of everything you have run so far. Instead of stacking fatigue inside a density block until the reps get ugly, you fire off a short, genuinely explosive set, then you rest until your breathing comes back, then you do it again, and again, fifteen times. Every single set is fast. None of them is a survival set. What gets trained is the alactic power system on top of the aerobic system that clears it, and the entire adaptation lives in how quickly you are ready to go again. That is why the recovery, not the set, is the measurement today. Then the treadmill takes the other half of hard. You are on tired legs, so the run goes vertical instead of fast: a grade ladder, low impact, high output, which is still the single best trade this program has found. Incline has not appeared since 08-02.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · DAY B · ANKLES, KNEES, HIPS
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day B · matched to tired legs and a grade ladder

items.name: SHOULDER PROTOCOL · 2 x 20
items.detail: Arm circles or dislocates with a towel, twenty forward and twenty back, twice. The snatch puts a bell overhead at speed a hundred and forty times today. This is the price of admission for that.

items.name: TOE SQUATS · 60 sec
items.detail: Kneel with the toes tucked under, sit back onto the heels, hold and breathe. Sixty seconds. If it is brutal, rock in and out of it instead of holding. This is straight at the plantar fascia and calves, which is what a twelve percent grade is going to ask for in half an hour.

items.name: ANKLE ROLLS IN A DEEP SQUAT · 45 sec
items.detail: Sit into the bottom of a squat, heels down if they will go, and drive each knee forward over the toes in turn, then circle the ankles. Forty-five seconds. Uphill running lives entirely in ankle dorsiflexion.

items.name: KNEE DRIVES AND SIDE STEP-UPS · 45 sec
items.detail: Standing knee drives, twenty a side, quick. Then lateral step-ups onto a bench or box, ten a side. Wakes the hip flexors and the frontal-plane hip up before you ask them to climb.

items.name: BELL PRIMER · 15 SWINGS + 5/5 HIGH PULL · 16 kg
items.detail: Fifteen two-hand swings with the light bell, then five high pulls per side. This is the rehearsal for the snatch, not a warm-up set. Feel the hips throw the bell and the arm do nothing but steer. If the high pull is floating to your chest by itself, the snatch will be easy.

blocks.text: Day B off the Moves Method menu because the day ends on a grade ladder and your legs came in tired. Day A ran on 08-17, Day C ran yesterday. Six minutes, not ten, because the budget is forty-five today and the main block is where it needs to go.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · A+A SNATCH REPEATS
blocks.meta: ~18 min · 20 kg bell · sets of 10 per arm · rest is prescribed by your breathing, not by a clock
blocks.format: alactic + aerobic repeats (StrongFirst A+A) — short powerful sets, full recovery between, many of them
blocks.workRest: Work is roughly 20 to 25 seconds. Rest is however long it takes your breathing to come back to conversational — usually 45 to 75 seconds. If it is taking longer than 90 seconds, you are going too hard or the sets are too long. Cut to sets of 8.

items.name: ONE-ARM SNATCH · 10 reps, one arm per set · 20 kg
items.detail: One set is ten snatches on one arm. Next set is the other arm. Alternate all the way through. The 20 kg is your proven working bell now, and it has never been snatched in this log. Hip snap hard, punch the hand through at the top so the bell lands quiet on the forearm, then throw it back down into the next rep. Every rep of every set is fast. There is no such thing as a slow snatch today.

items.name: TARGET · 14 SETS · floor 10, stretch 16
items.detail: Fourteen sets is 140 reps, seven per arm. That is a serious snatch day. If eighteen minutes runs out at ten sets, that is the honest number and we log it. If you are at fourteen with time left and the bell still feels light, take sixteen. Do not chase the number by shortening rest — the rest IS the training.

items.name: THE ONE RULE · NEVER LET A SET GET SLOW
items.detail: This is the entire discipline of A+A and it is the opposite of every density block you have run. The moment a set feels like grinding rather than throwing, you rested too little. Stop, take another thirty seconds, then go. You are training the power system and the aerobic engine that refuels it. You are deliberately NOT training the burn. Fifteen crisp sets beats twenty ugly ones by a mile.

items.name: COUNT ONE THING FOR ME
items.detail: Somewhere in the middle, after a set, count how many seconds until your breathing is back. Then do it again on the last set. If the two numbers are close, your aerobic recovery is strong. If the last one is double the first, that is the single most useful data point this block can produce and it sets where we start next time.

blocks.text: Neupert's #6, King-Sized Killer 2.0, is snatches in sets of five for twenty minutes, and it is a density block. This takes his movement and his bell and reorganizes it around the A+A principle instead: bigger sets, real recovery, quality defended over volume. Same exercise, completely different physiology, and a structure that has never appeared in this program.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE FURNACE · GRADE LADDER
blocks.meta: 10 min · treadmill · this is the hard run and it goes uphill, not fast
blocks.format: incline ladder — 5 climbs, 60 sec on, 60 sec walk recovery
blocks.workRest: 60 sec climbing, 60 sec walking at 5.5 to 6.0 km/h and 1 percent. Five times through. Do not sit down between, keep walking.

items.name: CLIMB 1 · 60 sec @ 6% grade @ 8.0 km/h
items.detail: 8.0 km/h is 7:30 per kilometre, a shade over 12 minutes per mile flat, which is deliberately slow on the flat and will not feel slow at six percent. Set the grade first, then the speed, and run tall with a short quick step.

items.name: CLIMB 2 · 60 sec @ 8% grade @ 8.0 km/h
items.detail: Same speed, more grade. This is the axis that actually works on you. Every version of a hard run this program has found that you respected came from grade, not from the speed dial.

items.name: CLIMB 3 · 60 sec @ 10% grade @ 8.0 km/h
items.detail: This one starts to bite. Lean from the ankles, not the waist. Do not grab the rails — if you need the rails, drop the grade two points and keep running honest.

items.name: CLIMB 4 · 60 sec @ 12% grade @ 8.0 km/h
items.detail: The top of the ladder. Twelve percent at 250 lb is a real load through the calves and the Achilles, and yesterday was already a lot of time on your feet. Sixty seconds is the whole reason this is safe. If the machine will not go past ten, hold ten and add half a km/h instead.

items.name: CLIMB 5 · 60 sec @ 10% grade, all-out effort
items.detail: Last one. Ten percent, and you pick the speed — whatever you can genuinely hold for sixty seconds and nothing left over. This is the only all-out piece in the session and it is at the very end on purpose. Note the speed you chose. It becomes the benchmark.

blocks.text: You ran 12 minutes continuous yesterday at your easy band, so today the run changes axis completely. Incline was the biggest single discovery in this whole log — a genuinely hard run at a fraction of the foot impact, and one you actually enjoy — and it has not been programmed since 08-02. On tired legs, on a day you asked to go hard, it is the obvious call. Tell me the belt distance and the Climb 5 speed; this machine still has no calibration on file.

blocks.title: BLOCK 3 · HAND-TO-HAND + MIDLINE
blocks.meta: ~8 min · 16 kg · the wildcard and the standing core block, run together

items.name: HAND-TO-HAND SWING · 20 reps  ·  WILDCARD
items.detail: One-arm swing, and at the top of the arc, when the bell is weightless for a beat, let go and catch it with the other hand. Twenty total. This has never appeared anywhere in this program. It punishes a lazy hip snap immediately, because the float only exists if the hips actually threw it, and it turns a swing into a grip and timing problem. Start slow, one switch at a time. Use the 16, not the 20.

items.name: PLANK DRAG-THROUGH · 10 per side · 20 kg
items.detail: High plank, feet wide, bell parked outside one hand. Reach under with the opposite hand and drag it across to the other side. Ten each way. The hips must not rotate — that is the whole exercise. Anti-rotation under load, with the shoulders already tired from a hundred and forty snatches.

items.name: HOLLOW ROCKS · 20 reps
items.detail: On your back, low back glued flat, arms and legs long, and rock as one rigid piece. Twenty. If the low back lifts, tuck the knees in and shorten the lever. Anti-extension, and it is nothing like anything you did yesterday.

blocks.text: Three rounds. The midline block is standing policy and it stays, but it is eight minutes today rather than ten, and the wildcard rides inside it rather than getting its own slot. Forty-five minutes is a real constraint and the snatches are where the day's money went.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · calves and forearms, which is where this session will show up tomorrow
blocks.text: Wall calf stretch, 45 seconds per side, straight leg then a soft knee to catch the soleus. That is the tax on the grade ladder and it is worth paying now. Forearm and wrist extensor stretch, 30 seconds per side, palm down, gently pull the fingers back — a hundred and forty snatches plus hand-to-hand swings is a lot of grip. Half-kneeling hip flexor, 45 seconds a side. Then a minute of slow nasal breathing, longer out than in, standing or lying, and you are done.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM today. Block 1 is deliberately NOT on a clock — start the countdown for 18 minutes as a container, but each set starts when your breathing comes back, not when the second hand says so. Use the countdown properly for Block 2: 60 seconds on, 60 seconds off, ten minutes total.
